## Private compact-cell interleaving

`GAGP_GPU_PRIVATE_CELL_SOA=1` changes only the physical layout of an admitted
private compact IntList arena. Within each physical CUDA block, lane `t` stores
its logical cell `i` at `block_base + i * block_width + t`. Each lane retains
the same logical capacity; total allocation, list handles, allocation charges,
overflow/replay decisions and frame/memo ownership keep their existing rules.
Program scheduling cannot transfer a block's scratch columns to another block.

Private spans carry a stride for compact local cells. Immutable boxed input and
answer tables remain contiguous. Singleton, concat, slicing, indexing, and
resident scoring respect the stride; restoring the logical cell cursor restores
the same lifetime boundary. Cooperative contiguous copying is used only when
both source and target are contiguous. A strided copy uses the ordinary owner
loop. The option declines when compact private-list admission is unavailable,
and `execution_profile` records `private-cell-soa` or `private-cell-soa-declined`.

The ownership/boundary checks are in `private_intlist_offset_checks.cuh` through
`gagp_test_extended_payload_gpu`: one-lane and 32-lane boxed/compact storage,
contiguous/interleaved local cells, nested windows, wide integers, resident
distance scores, cursor restoration and logical/physical overflow. The
`gagp_test_gpu_phase_population` private-owner evolution fixtures also enable
the option while retaining their CPU and genotype checks. Test commands and
measured speed are recorded separately; enabling this layout is not a speed
claim.

## Private short-pattern edit distance

`GAGP_GPU_SHORT_EDIT_DISTANCE=1` enables an exact scoring path for private
IntList Levenshtein fitness. Session initialization prepares a sorted dictionary
of full signed Int64 values and 64-bit position masks from the same decoded,
immutable answer cache used for GPU upload. Each original case retains its own
descriptor, so input-case permutations still select the correct answer. Session
reinitialization clears/rebuilds the tables and invalidates prior fitness reuse.
Preparation and upload remain inside the ordinary initialization timing; these
immutable answer tables do not reduce the configured payload workspace cap.

Whole-sequence distance for answers of at most 64 elements uses a one-word
bit-vector update, with the global-alignment boundary. Longer answers retain
the original full DP; inputs are never truncated. Equal and empty sequences
have exact shortcuts after the existing answer-length and penalty guards.
The result still uses the same capped/discounted conversion and wrong-count
rules. Evaluation fuel, payload allocations, errors, genotype operators and RNG
are unaffected by this post-execution scoring calculation.

Descriptors must match the expected raw tag/token/marker and decoded length,
with in-bounds dictionary entries. Internal/private-marker answers decline
dictionary preparation and keep ordinary scoring. The runtime does not trust
caller-supplied program metadata for this optimization. The word update follows
[Myers (1999)](https://doi.org/10.1145/316542.316550), applied here to full-width
integer equality rather than a byte alphabet.

The implementation is in `short_edit_distance.hpp`, `short_edit_patterns.hpp`
and `device/short_edit_device.cuh` under `cpp/src/runtime/gpu/`. Runtime tests
include `gagp_test_extended_payload_gpu` for 0/63/64/65-element labels, wide
integers, capped/discounted scores, case ordering and reinitialization, and
`gagp_test_gpu_phase_population` for native CPU checks of evolving list phases.
Actual test results and full-search speed remain separate evidence.

- Optional `GAGP_GPU_PRIVATE_CELL_SOA`: private compact-cell layout admission in
  `runtime/gpu/fitness_gpu.cu`, physical block columns in `device/kernels.cuh`,
  strided private spans/copies in `device/builtins_device.cuh`, state setup in
  `device/execute_bytecode_device.cuh`; workspace fields in
  `cpp/include/gagp/runtime/gpu/region_types_gpu.hpp`. Check
  `gagp_test_extended_payload_gpu` and `gagp_test_gpu_phase_population`;
  ownership/capacity rules are in `docs/design/payload.md`. Runtime paths above
  are relative to `cpp/src/`.

- Optional `GAGP_GPU_SHORT_EDIT_DISTANCE`: `runtime/gpu/fitness_gpu.cu` prepares
  immutable per-case masks through `short_edit_patterns.hpp`; workspace pointers
  pass through `device/execute_bytecode_device.cuh` to `resident_score_device.cuh`
  and `short_edit_device.cuh`. The full-width one-word update and identity/range
  checks are in `short_edit_distance.hpp`; long labels retain ordinary DP.
  Tests: `gagp_test_extended_payload_gpu`, `gagp_test_gpu_phase_population`;
  contract: `docs/design/payload.md`. Paths are relative to `cpp/src/`.

- `GAGP_FUSED_COLD_EXECUTABLE=1` returns the executable from the admission that
  just validated it, avoiding a second identity serialization. The same private
  cold-proof owners enforce actual input order, registry raw values and snapshot
  publication; `repro/gpu/phase_layout.hpp` consumes the artifact. GPU bytecode
  checks remain unchanged. Tests: `gagp_test_grammar_membership`,
  `gagp_test_gpu_phase_population`.

`GAGP_FUSED_COLD_EXECUTABLE=1` lets that same admission return its already
validated immutable executable, avoiding another full identity serialization.
The private accessor runs only after the current invocation either checked the
complete certificate identity or constructed a fresh certificate. It still
checks the actual evaluator input order. Registry constants additionally require
the current read scope and exact raw tags/bits/markers; speculative artifacts
remain inside the existing snapshot until its reads validate. Scalar-only
admission can return its private artifact without a registry transaction.
Missing artifacts and mismatched input order retain ordinary lowering. Public
registry lookup and GPU bytecode/physical-capacity verification are unchanged.
Tests: `gagp_test_grammar_membership`, `gagp_test_gpu_phase_population`, including
stale scalar provenance, registry aliases, disabled flags, reordered inputs and
multi-generation full CPU/AST checks on staged and window paths.

`GAGP_GPU_PARENT_FITNESS_CACHE=1` additionally indexes every previous-generation
genotype on the GPU. It requires unchanged-fitness reuse and is also fixed at
owner construction. A post-elite child that differs from its selected parent
may inherit another parent's completed score only after every phase node,
origin, constant tag, raw numeric bits and boolean flag compares equal. The
fixed region skeleton and decoding context belong to the same private owner.
Hashes locate candidates; hash equality alone never authorizes reuse. Up to64
open-addressing probes are attempted; collisions or saturation can decline
reuse and retain ordinary evaluation. The table is rebuilt before stage-storage
overwrites the previous-generation trees. Its buffers are outside the shared
scratch bank and included in resident-byte accounting (256KiB at P16384).

The same successful-score/session-revision/generation guards above still apply.
Index construction and exact lookup are charged to reproduction time. Selection,
variation, RNG and offspring remain unchanged. The phase-population test includes
forced hash collisions, full-table misses, signed-zero and individual genotype
field differences, plus full CPU/AST comparisons across generations and session
changes. This opt-in is experimental; admission and measured gains are recorded
per immutable study attempt.

Optional cross-parent lookup uses `evolution/repro/gpu/parent_fitness_cache.cuh`:
  GPU hashes locate candidates, full genotype equality authorizes reuse, and
  session/generation guards remain in `completed_fitness_reuse.hpp`.
